value.title: Deliverables: owners, stages and write-back (workstream 008 s06)
value.summary: Each deliverable a pod template names has an owner role and stages; the first stage is recorded while a late member keeps working; a recorded stage is sent as one request to the role the template names for write-back, which outlives the pod.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Each deliverable a pod template names has an owner role and stages; the first stage is recorded while a late member keeps working; a recorded stage is sent as one request to the role the template names for write-back, which outlives the pod.

sections.name: goals
value: A pod's result has an owner, is not held up by its slowest member, and reaches the seat that keeps the knowledge.

sections.name: non_goals
value: Changing how outputs are recorded (`pij output`).

value.claim: `pij pod show` lists each deliverable with its owner role and that role's live holder; plan and up warn when the owner role does not exist, with the add command.

`pij pod stage <pod> <deliverable> <stage> --output <path>` records a stage in the pod folder when the members it needs are done; a later stage folds in a late member's work. show lists which stages are recorded and which member each open stage waits on.

When a stage is recorded and the template names a write-back role for the deliverable, pij sends its result to that role as one request (send to a role, PRD 001) and logs it; the request stays with that role after the pod goes down.
Cost: one writer commit per stage and one request per write-back. No loop, poll or timer.

value.title: Deliverables: owners, stages and write-back (workstream 008 s06)

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: Send to a role and its queue (crates/daemon/src/delivery/role_send.rs); outputs (community/output.rs); the pod folder (plan 247).

value.risk: The write-back role has no live holder.
value.mitigation: The request queues for the role, as any send to a role does.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Cost: one writer commit per stage and one request per write-back; no loop, poll or timer.
No permission rule changes (PRD 003); no daemon enforcement of a type's rules; no existing JSON field removed or renamed.
Builds nice-19 through `just shared-build`, one at a time.
